notes: Visual reference dimensions are explicitly classified as Structure, Visual Language, or cross-cutting. Existing dimension ids remain stable for backward compatibility; new evaluations may add tone-manner and typography-character. A reference can be authoritative for one dimension without owning the whole artifact.

dimensions.asks: How many distinct information units does the image carry, relative to its family (thumbnail: 1 dominant idea + 1-2 supports; body infographic: 2-4 modules)?
dimensions.adopt_signal: Density matched to the family's target, not maximized.
dimensions.imitation_risk: low — a target range, not an expression

dimensions.asks: How much visual chrome (icons, cards, mini-charts) competes for attention independent of the information it carries?
dimensions.adopt_signal: Low-to-medium chrome even when semantic density is medium/high (SUENGJ-ARTICLE-IMAGE-FAMILIES.md §4.2).

dimensions.asks: Is there one clear reading path, or several competing first-reads?
dimensions.adopt_signal: A first-read payload legible in 2-5 seconds (VISUAL-INFORMATION-GAIN.md §5).
dimensions.imitation_risk: low — hierarchy discipline transfers across unrelated subject matter

dimensions.asks: Does the arrangement feel designed as one composition, or assembled from independent parts?
dimensions.adopt_signal: Fewer, larger compositional groups; asymmetry that still balances (SUENGJ-VISUAL-TASTE-CALIBRATION.md §1).
dimensions.imitation_risk: high — a specific composition is usually the reference's own expression, not a transferable principle

dimensions.asks: Does negative space do work, or is it filled to look complete?
dimensions.adopt_signal: Generous negative space that is not filled merely because it is empty (SUENGJ-VISUAL-TASTE-CALIBRATION.md §4).

dimensions.asks: What overall editorial impression does the visual carry — calm/research-led, executive/analytical, promotional, playful, or another explicitly justified register?
dimensions.adopt_signal: A transferable tonal relationship that can apply across artifacts without importing the reference's layout or literal identity.
dimensions.imitation_risk: medium — describe the tonal behavior, not a brand slogan or literal campaign look

dimensions.asks: What typographic character supports the hierarchy — quiet editorial, compact report, expressive display, or another role-based treatment — independent of exact font files?
dimensions.adopt_signal: Role-based typography character and hierarchy, not a copied font file or proprietary typeface.
dimensions.imitation_risk: medium — exact proprietary fonts remain renderer/project assets, not Core reference content

dimensions.asks: Does color carry a semantic role (structure, accent, warning), or is it decorative?
dimensions.imitation_risk: high — an exact palette is usually a house identity, not a reusable principle; note the role it plays instead of the hex values

dimensions.asks: Is linework thin and quiet, and is any material depth subtle rather than glossy/cinematic?
dimensions.adopt_signal: Thin structural rules, no heavy shadow or glossy 3D (SUENGJ-VISUAL-TASTE-CALIBRATION.md §2).

dimensions.asks: Does the family's text rule hold — no baked-in mutable copy in a thumbnail, stable semantic labels only where they earn their place in a body infographic (SUENGJ-ARTICLE-IMAGE-FAMILIES.md §3.3, §4.3)?
dimensions.adopt_signal: Text used exactly where the family contract allows it.

dimensions.asks: What is this reference actually authoritative for — thumbnail, body infographic, both, or neither?
dimensions.adopt_signal: A named artifact family this evaluation's evidence actually supports.
dimensions.imitation_risk: low — this dimension exists to bound the other dimensions, not to be adopted itself

dimensions.asks: Does information density and label/legend use match a named audience's expertise (V2-EDITORIAL-LEARNING-CORE.md §3 table)?
dimensions.adopt_signal: Density that would change if the audience changed.

not_authoritative_for: A good thumbnail is not evidence about body-infographic density, and vice versa — see SUENGJ-ARTICLE-IMAGE-FAMILIES.md §1.

Exact evidence values, axes, or chronology — those remain deterministic per SUENGJ-ARTICLE-IMAGE-FAMILIES.md §4.5 and editorial/RIGHTS-AND-PROVENANCE.md §3; a visual reference may inform style, never invent evidence.
Whether a visual should exist at all — that is the information-gain gate in VISUAL-INFORMATION-GAIN.md, not this profile.
selection_hints: Match applicable_to.artifacts to the requested visual/* artifact before matching palette or composition — a body-infographic evaluation is weak selection evidence for a thumbnail request.

Prefer evaluations whose dimensions include at least one adopt verdict specific to the requested artifact family; a reference evaluated only as do_not_copy across the board is evidence to avoid imitation, not evidence to select toward generation.
composition and palette-colour-role are the two dimensions most often do_not_copy; do not select a reference primarily for these unless the evaluation explicitly marks them adopt.
Resolve Structure dimensions before Visual Language dimensions. A composition/hierarchy reference does not implicitly grant palette authority, and a palette/tone reference does not imply its layout.
Use authoritative_override only for the specific visual-language dimension that is intended to outrank the brand default; do not treat one approved trait as authority over the whole reference.

layer_model.structure: Message arrangement and comprehension geometry: density, hierarchy, composition, text strategy, artifact/audience fit.
layer_model.visual_language: Expressive treatment after Structure is stable: tone, palette, typography character, spacing, line/shape, materiality/depth.
layer_model.cross_cutting: Constraints that touch both layers but must not let visual preference rewrite semantic structure.
